name: GBIF (Global Biodiversity Information Facility)
description: Over three billion species occurrence records - a specimen in a museum drawer, a bird logged on eBird, a plant photographed on iNaturalist - each with species, date and coordinates, from more than 2,000 publishing institutions. The single largest open record of where life has been observed.

license.name: per-record: CC0, CC-BY or CC-BY-NC
license.redistribution: honour each record's licence; a download DOI is minted for citation

access.auth_note: searching is anonymous; large downloads need a free GBIF account and are delivered asynchronously with a DOI
access.size_hint: a full-species download can be several GB
access.rate_limit: search API is limited to 100,000 records via paging - past that you must use the download API
access.pagination: offset and limit, offset capped at 100,000

probes.description: Resolve a loose name to the accepted taxon

recipes.title: Occurrences of one species in a bounding box
recipes.code:
KEY=$(curl -s 'https://api.gbif.org/v1/species/match?name=Danaus%20plexippus' | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["usageKey"])')
curl -s "https://api.gbif.org/v1/occurrence/search?taxonKey=$KEY&decimalLatitude=38,40&decimalLongitude=-78,-76&limit=5" | python3 -m json.tool | head -30

recipes.title: Daily histogram for one species, one box, one month
Observer-effort denominator: the same query for all birds
recipes.code:
# Swap taxonKey for classKey=212 (Aves) to get every bird record in the same box on the
# same days. Dividing by this is what makes counts comparable across years: the DC box
# logged 210 hummingbird records in 2000 and 13,261 in 2024 -- observers, not birds.
curl -s 'https://api.gbif.org/v1/occurrence/search?classKey=212&decimalLatitude=38.5,39.5&decimalLongitude=-77.6,-76.5&year=2024&month=5&limit=0&facet=day&facetLimit=31&basisOfRecord=HUMAN_OBSERVATION'

gotchas.trap: Paging past 100,000 records silently stops rather than erroring.
gotchas.fix: Use the asynchronous download API for anything larger; it returns a DOI you can cite.

gotchas.trap: Occurrence records include cultivated plants, zoo animals and fossils.
gotchas.fix: Filter on basisOfRecord and establishmentMeans before treating hits as wild observations.

gotchas.trap: Coordinates are often rounded or obscured for endangered species.
occurrence/search accepts facet=day alongside year= and month=, which is easy to miss.
gotchas.fix: One call then returns a full daily histogram for that month. Building a day-resolution seasonal curve by looping eventDate day by day costs ~30x more requests: faceting by day over month+year collapsed a 150,000-call job to 5,250.

gotchas.trap: eBird's annual export reaches GBIF about a year late, so the most recent year looks catastrophically empty rather than merely incomplete.
gotchas.fix: Checked 2026-09-07: the DC box held 422 Ruby-throated Hummingbird records for 2025 against 13,261 for 2024. Any seasonal-timing measure reads that as a wildly early season. Compare each year's volume against the trailing median and drop the incomplete tail; never trust the current or previous calendar year.

gotchas.trap: More than about 6 concurrent search requests get silently throttled, failing even after five retries with exponential backoff.
gotchas.fix: 10 threads failed 198 of 4,362 histogram calls (4.5%). The identical job list at 4 threads refetched all 198 with zero errors at the same ~250 requests/min. Concurrency above ~6 buys no throughput and loses data.

gotchas.trap: A burst of rapid sequential calls occasionally answers HTTP 200 with a JSON *array* error body instead of the search object.
gotchas.fix: Parse defensively and treat a non-dict body as retryable. Code that goes straight to d['count'] dies with 'list indices must be integers' thousands of calls into a harvest.

gotchas.trap: Occurrence counts fold in museum specimens and fossils whose collection dates say nothing about present-day seasonal timing.
gotchas.fix: Filter basisOfRecord=HUMAN_OBSERVATION for anything phenological. This is the same trap as the existing cultivated/zoo gotcha, but it bites date-based work rather than range maps.
